name: gizza-ai/browser-history-parser
summary: Parse a Chrome or Firefox history database into a visit timeline

tool.description: Parse an uploaded browser history database into a unified, searchable visit timeline. Auto-detects Chrome/Edge (a `History` file: urls + visits tables) or Firefox (`places.sqlite`: moz_places + moz_historyvisits) by reading the on-disk SQLite file directly (no SQL engine, read-only). Each row has a readable UTC timestamp, URL, page title, visit type (link/typed/bookmark/reload/…), and visit count. Provide the file via `url` (a public http/https link) or `ref` (an uploaded attachment id). Filter by a URL/title substring (`search`), sort newest or oldest (`order`), cap the rows (`limit`), and export as json or csv.

format.description: Output format: json (structured, the default) or csv (a spreadsheet-friendly table with a browser column so exports from several history files merge).

limit.description: Maximum number of visits to return; 0 means all visits. Default 0.

order.description: Timeline sort order by visit time: newest (most recent first, the default) or oldest.

ref.description: Reference id from a prior tool call. Use either url or ref.

search.description: Only include visits whose URL or page title contains this text (case-insensitive). Omit to return every visit.

url.description: Document URL (HTTP/HTTPS). Use either url or ref.
